Description

Deleting a project (ToolsQA_DeleteNet_1790762899640) must fire a 'POST https://regpluswta.api.kaz.com.bd/api/Project/Delete' request with HTTP 200, and the project must be genuinely gone from the account afterwards (re-fetched via the app's own follow-up GetProjects call, not just the UI's optimistic removal). NOTE (confirmed live - see pages/tools_projects_page.py): the Delete response body shape differs from Create/Rename ('{"isSuccess":<bool>,"error":...}'), and 'isSuccess' has been observed to intermittently report false (an EF Core DbContext-threading error) even when the project was in fact removed - so this test treats HTTP 200 plus the project's real absence from the next GetProjects response as the authoritative pass condition, not the possibly-flaky 'isSuccess' field alone.

Precondition

User is logged in and on Tools > Projects.

Test Data

Project name: ToolsQA_DeleteNet_1790762899640

Steps

1. Log in and open Tools > Projects 2. Create a project named 'ToolsQA_DeleteNet_1790762899640' 3. Delete it while capturing the Delete request and the follow-up GetProjects response 4. Verify status 200 and the project's real absence from GetProjects

Expected Result

Deleting a project (ToolsQA_DeleteNet_1790762899640) must fire a 'POST https://regpluswta.api.kaz.com.bd/api/Project/Delete' request with HTTP 200, and the project must be genuinely gone from the account afterwards (re-fetched via the app's own follow-up GetProjects call, not just the UI's optimistic removal). NOTE (confirmed live - see pages/tools_projects_page.py): the Delete response body shape differs from Create/Rename ('{"isSuccess":<bool>,"error":...}'), and 'isSuccess' has been observed to intermittently report false (an EF Core DbContext-threading error) even when the project was in fact removed - so this test treats HTTP 200 plus the project's real absence from the next GetProjects response as the authoritative pass condition, not the possibly-flaky 'isSuccess' field alone.

Actual Result

Deleting 'ToolsQA_DeleteNet_1790762899640' correctly returned HTTP 200 and the project was genuinely gone from GetProjects afterwards (isSuccess reported as False).

Creating a second project with the exact same name as an existing one ('ToolsQA_Dup_1790762944796') is confirmed live to be blocked at the data level - CreateProject responds '{"id":0,"hasError":true,"errorMessage":"Please choose another name"}' and no duplicate row is created. However, this is ALSO confirmed live to be a real UX gap: the modal simply closes with zero visible feedback to the user (no toast, no inline error) - the rejection is silent. Both are documented and asserted: the app correctly prevents duplicate DATA, but gives the user no correct signal that their second attempt failed.

After creating a project ('ToolsQA_Persist_1790762971722'), reloading the page must still show it - proving the save is real server-side persistence, not just an optimistic client-side UI update. Confirmed live: unlike a fresh external 'page.goto("/wta/Project")' (which redirects to /wta/Information per the documented Tools deep-link gotcha), 'page.reload()' from an already-open /wta/Project page stays on /wta/Project and re-fetches the list from the server, so this test uses reload() rather than re-navigating through the Tools menu.

After creating a project ('ToolsQA_Persist_1790762971722'), reloading the page must still show it - proving the save is real server-side persistence, not just an optimistic client-side UI update. Confirmed live: unlike a fresh external 'page.goto("/wta/Project")' (which redirects to /wta/Information per the documented Tools deep-link gotcha), 'page.reload()' from an already-open /wta/Project page stays on /wta/Project and re-fetches the list from the server, so this test uses reload() rather than re-navigating through the Tools menu.

Actual Result

'ToolsQA_Persist_1790762971722' correctly survived a page reload, staying on https://regplus.kaz.com.bd/wta/Project - proving real server-side persistence.
